note: Canonical Writing Model — domain-specific pedagogical knowledge, loaded as DATA by the domain-independent Developmental Guide Engine. These are culturally established FUNCTIONS of effective writing and cultural RESOURCES the engine uses to interpret student writing. They are NOT developmental stages, NOT a required instructional sequence, and NOT rigid templates. The engine must decide which domains are currently relevant; it must never force students through the domains in a predetermined order.

functional_evaluation_questions: What is the writer trying to accomplish?
possible_differentiations: distinguishing what is said from what it is for
distinguishing assignment compliance from communicative intent
possible_integrations: aligning every section to one purpose
common_productive_tensions: a topic is present but no purpose is yet visible
purpose stated but not sustained across the essay
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask the writer to state, in one sentence, what they want the reader to understand or do
invite the writer to check whether each part serves that purpose

possible_differentiations: separating what the writer knows from what the reader knows
distinguishing insider shorthand from reader-ready explanation
possible_integrations: shaping openings and evidence to reader needs
common_productive_tensions: writer assumes knowledge the reader lacks
over-explaining what the reader already knows
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask the writer to imagine a specific reader and what that reader would need first
invite the writer to mark where a newcomer might get lost

domain_status.description: Culturally available functions and resources for beginning an essay.
is_not: a checklist every introduction must satisfy
a rule that the thesis must appear in a particular location
must_be_interpreted_relative_to: the central problem, question, claim, or experience
the organization of the developing whole essay

domains.governing_communicative_function: Prepare a reader to enter the essay's developing world of meaning — help the reader understand enough of the subject, situation, question, problem, experience, or argument to follow what comes next. The exact work required depends on the essay's purpose and genre.
communicative_functions: prepare or state a central claim
indicate the direction of the essay
possible_communicative_functions: distinguish the specific focus from the broader topic
establish common ground with the reader
introduce a tension, contradiction, puzzle, or uncertainty
indicate the direction of the essay
establish the relationship between writer and audience
create expectations appropriate to the genre
domains.engine_note_on_functions: Do not assume that every opening needs to perform every function.
reader_needs: knowing what the essay is about
knowing which part of a broad topic matters
knowing whose perspective is being represented
understanding why the writer is addressing the issue
knowing what kind of essay is beginning
receiving enough orientation to interpret the next paragraph
being given a reason to continue reading
domains.reader_needs_note: These are interpretive possibilities, not mandatory requirements.
domains.resources_note: Introduce a resource only when it serves the student's operative purpose and the needs of the reader. No resource is automatically required.

observable_organizations.name: Topic naming
observable_organizations.description: Identifies a general subject but has not yet differentiated a specific focus, problem, question, or purpose.
observable_organizations.example: Social media is an important part of life today.

observable_organizations.name: Topic plus context
observable_organizations.description: Identifies a subject and supplies background, but the reader may not yet know why the subject matters.

observable_organizations.name: Topic plus position
observable_organizations.description: States an opinion or claim quickly, but the conceptual context or significance may remain unclear.

observable_organizations.name: Situation without explicit purpose
observable_organizations.description: Creates a scene, anecdote, or example, but its relationship to the essay's larger purpose is not yet visible.

observable_organizations.name: Problem framing
observable_organizations.description: Identifies a conflict, tension, difficulty, or unresolved issue that organizes the opening.

observable_organizations.name: Question framing
observable_organizations.description: Organizes the opening around a question or puzzle.

observable_organizations.name: Significance framing
observable_organizations.description: Establishes why a subject, problem, or question matters.

observable_organizations.name: Reader-oriented framing
observable_organizations.description: Anticipates what the reader needs to understand before encountering the central claim.

observable_organizations.name: Integrated opening
observable_organizations.description: Coordinates several functions (topic, context, problem, significance, direction) into a coherent beginning.

observable_organizations.name: Deliberately indirect opening
observable_organizations.description: Begins through narrative, image, scene, or conceptual exploration and delays explicit framing for a purposeful reason. Do not assume indirect organization is deficient.

observable_organizations.name: Overloaded opening
observable_organizations.description: Attempts too many functions or introduces too many ideas before a governing purpose becomes clear.

observable_organizations.name: Formula-driven opening
observable_organizations.description: Visibly follows a learned template, but the elements may not yet function together meaningfully.

domains.observable_organizations_note: These are possible descriptive organizations, not stages and not exhaustive categories.
possible_differentiations: interesting detail from functionally relevant detail
anecdote from the meaning it is meant to establish
an assignment prompt from the writer's own operative purpose
a position from the reasons the position matters
background needed by the reader from background that merely delays the essay
a conventional opening resource from the communicative function it serves
possible_integrations: question with the direction of the essay
the opening with the anticipated whole essay
several opening functions into one coherent movement
an unconventional beginning with a clear eventual direction
possible_coordinations: the assignment and the writer's own purpose
the broad topic and the essay's specific focus
the opening and the thesis or central claim
the opening and the first body section
the writer's knowledge and the reader's likely knowledge
multiple ideas under a governing purpose
common_productive_tensions: The topic is present, but the purpose is not yet visible.
Context is present, but the problem or question remains undifferentiated.
The problem is visible, but the reader does not yet know why it matters.
Significance is asserted in broad language but not grounded.
The writer has a purpose, but the opening does not yet prepare the reader for it.
The writer assumes knowledge the reader may not possess.
The writer supplies excessive background before establishing direction.
The writer states a thesis before the reader has enough context to understand it.
The writer delays the thesis purposefully, but the connection between opening and essay remains uncertain.
An anecdote is engaging but disconnected from the essay's purpose.
A question is posed, but the essay does not appear organized around answering it.
The opening contains several potentially useful ideas that have not yet been coordinated.
The opening follows a recognizable formula, but its parts do not function together.
The opening is clear but does not yet establish stakes.
The opening is interesting but not orienting.
The opening is informative but not purposeful.
The writer's operative purpose differs from the apparent purpose of the assignment.
domains.tensions_note: Identify only ONE primary tension at a time.

possible_meanings: the writer has not yet formed a central claim
the writer is deliberately delaying the claim
the genre does not require an early explicit thesis
the writer assumes the direction is already obvious
the teacher's task does not yet call for the thesis
the writer is postponing the central problem
the writer is still discovering the purpose
the writer has difficulty selecting relevant information
the writer has not differentiated the focus
the student does not yet understand the assignment
the submitted passage is only part of the opening

domains.alternative_interpretations_note: Do not collapse uncertainty into a single confident diagnosis.
common_misunderstandings: Every introduction must begin with a hook.
A hook is any dramatic or surprising sentence, regardless of relevance.
Every introduction must follow hook -> background -> thesis.
The thesis must always be the final sentence of the first paragraph.
The opening should begin as broadly as possible.
A dictionary definition automatically provides useful orientation.
A rhetorical question automatically creates interest.
The writer should hide the purpose to create suspense.
The introduction is merely a place to summarize the essay.
Context means including everything the writer knows.
Significance can be established by saying a topic is 'important'.
An anecdote is effective simply because it is personal or vivid.
The opening can be evaluated independently from the rest of the essay.
domains.misunderstandings_note: Be alert to these but do not automatically assume them.
possible_developmental_movements: from naming a topic to identifying a specific focus
from identifying a focus to framing a problem or question
from presenting information to orienting a reader
from asserting importance to establishing specific significance
from supplying background to selecting relevant context
from presenting an anecdote to clarifying its function
from stating a claim to preparing the reader to understand the claim
from following a template to using resources purposefully
from several disconnected opening functions to a coordinated movement
from writer-centered presentation to reader-oriented communication
from vague purpose to intentional control over what the opening is doing
from treating the opening as an isolated paragraph to coordinating it with the whole essay
domains.movements_note: These are possible reorganizations, not a required progression.

identify the specific problem within the broad topic
explain why the subject matters to the intended reader
identify what a naive reader needs to know first
distinguish background that is necessary from background that is merely available
explain the relationship between an anecdote and the essay's purpose
identify the question the essay is trying to answer
name what is at stake
compare two possible ways to frame the topic
explain why the introduction begins where it does
identify what the opening leads the reader to expect
check whether the opening prepares the reader for the central claim
revise one part of the opening to make its function clearer
explain what changed after a revision and why
identify which sentence currently does the most important work
decide which of several opening ideas should govern the others
imagine where a naive reader might become confused

domains.invitations_note: Invitations should require the student to think, explain, choose, or revise. Present only one at a time.

three_parts: Brief recognition of an observable feature in the student's participation
Connection to the current communicative purpose
One intellectual or writing action for the student to perform
invitation_construction_rules.example_form: You have established that school phone rules vary. To help a reader understand why that matters, identify the specific problem those differences create.
cautions: Do not use the example as a fixed verbal template.
Do not generate a replacement sentence for the student.

relationship_notes.Whole Essay Purpose: Interpret the opening in relation to what the whole essay is trying to accomplish.
relationship_notes.Audience Awareness: The opening helps establish what the reader needs in order to enter the essay.
relationship_notes.Central Claim / Thesis: The opening may state, prepare, complicate, or deliberately delay the central claim.
relationship_notes.Organization: The opening establishes expectations for the movement of the essay.
relationship_notes.Paragraph Purpose: An introductory paragraph may perform one or several coordinated functions.
relationship_notes.Word Choice and Voice: The opening often establishes tone, stance, and the writer-reader relationship.
relationship_notes.Revision and Reflective Control: The student's explanation of why an opening changed is evidence of intentional control.

genre_sensitivity.note: Do not apply one introduction model to all genres. Reason from the actual assignment and teacher purpose rather than infer genre solely from surface form.
genre_sensitivity.argumentative: May orient the reader to an issue, establish stakes, frame a problem, and prepare or state a claim.
genre_sensitivity.expository: May define the topic, establish scope, orient the reader, and indicate the organizing purpose.
genre_sensitivity.analytical: May identify an object of analysis, establish a conceptual problem, and prepare an interpretation.
genre_sensitivity.research: May establish context, identify a research problem, define scope, explain significance, and introduce a guiding claim or question.
genre_sensitivity.personal: May establish a voice, situation, experience, or tension without immediately stating an explicit thesis.
genre_sensitivity.narrative: May establish scene, character, conflict, perspective, or narrative expectation.
genre_sensitivity.reflective: May establish an experience, question, uncertainty, or transformation to be explored.
genre_sensitivity.literary_analysis: May introduce the work, establish an interpretive issue, and orient the reader toward a claim.

domains.inside_outside_coordination: Begin by interpreting the organization already present in the student's writing. Distinguish among the student's operative purpose, the assigned purpose, the teacher's pedagogical purpose, the reader's needs, and the cultural resources for openings. A mismatch must not automatically be treated as a student deficit — it may indicate unclear assignment expectations, a different student purpose, a reasonable alternative organization, insufficient reader orientation, an unfinished draft, tension between genre expectations and writer intention, or a need to clarify the immediate task. The next invitation should extend, differentiate, integrate, or productively challenge the student's present organization, not replace it with a conventional formula.
prohibitions: require a thesis in the final sentence
require all opening functions to appear
assume every opening is one paragraph
reject an unconventional beginning merely because it is unconventional
evaluate the opening without reference to purpose, audience, genre, and the developing whole
provide a polished model introduction for the student to imitate
classify the student into a stage or level
infer a stable writing ability from one introduction
treat the canonical domain as a rubric or grading checklist

functional_evaluation_questions: What claim appears to organize the essay?
possible_differentiations: separating a claim from a topic
distinguishing an arguable position from a statement of fact
possible_integrations: coordinating claim with evidence and reasoning
common_productive_tensions: multiple implicit claims compete for control
claim is present but too broad to organize the essay
candidate_developmental_invitations: invite the writer to name the one idea the whole essay is trying to establish
ask whether each paragraph advances that claim

functional_evaluation_questions: What purpose is this paragraph serving?
possible_differentiations: separating one paragraph's job from another's
possible_integrations: subordinating sentences to a single paragraph purpose
linking paragraph purpose to the thesis
common_productive_tensions: a paragraph tries to do several jobs at once
sentences list ideas without a governing purpose
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask what single job this paragraph is meant to do
invite the writer to test whether each sentence serves that job

functional_evaluation_questions: Is evidence connected to the claim?
possible_integrations: binding evidence to the claim it supports
common_productive_tensions: claims asserted without support
evidence present but its relevance is unstated
candidate_developmental_invitations: invite the writer to add a concrete instance that a skeptic would accept
ask how a specific piece of evidence supports the claim

possible_differentiations: separating description of evidence from analysis of it
possible_integrations: linking evidence, reasoning, and claim into one movement
common_productive_tensions: evidence is dropped in without explanation
reasoning is implied but never stated
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask the writer to explain what a piece of evidence shows and why
invite the writer to make the 'because' visible

functional_evaluation_questions: Why does each section follow the previous one?
Does the organization support the purpose?
possible_differentiations: distinguishing a list from a progression
possible_integrations: subordinating parts to a whole structure
common_productive_tensions: ideas are present but their order is arbitrary
structure fights the purpose
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask why one part comes before another
invite the writer to test whether reordering changes meaning

functional_evaluation_questions: Are transitions merely verbal or conceptual?
possible_differentiations: separating verbal connectors from conceptual connections
distinguishing addition from contrast from causation
common_productive_tensions: transition words present but no real conceptual link
ideas jump without signaling the relationship
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask what the actual relationship is between two adjacent ideas
invite the writer to name the connection rather than only label it

functional_evaluation_questions: Does it complete the communicative purpose?
possible_integrations: returning to purpose while extending it
connecting the ending back to the opening problem
common_productive_tensions: conclusion restates without adding meaning
significance is claimed but not developed
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask what the reader should now understand that they did not before
invite the writer to extend rather than repeat the main idea

possible_differentiations: separating main from subordinate ideas at the sentence level
possible_integrations: using syntax to foreground the most important idea
coordinating sentence form with paragraph purpose
common_productive_tensions: important ideas buried in subordinate positions
uniform sentences flatten emphasis
candidate_developmental_invitations: invite the writer to place the key idea in the emphatic position
ask which part of a sentence the reader should notice most

functional_evaluation_questions: Are words serving the intended purpose?
possible_differentiations: distinguishing tone appropriate to different readers
possible_integrations: aligning diction with purpose and audience
common_productive_tensions: vague wording obscures a precise idea
tone mismatched to the intended reader
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask whether a chosen word says exactly what is meant
invite the writer to consider how the tone lands for the intended reader

possible_integrations: connecting revision decisions to purpose and audience
common_productive_tensions: changes made without a reason tied to purpose
revision touches surface but not organization
candidate_developmental_invitations: ask the writer what they changed and why it serves the purpose
invite the writer to reflect on whether a revision improved communication
